what_its_for: Flurandrenolide is a steroid cream, lotion, ointment, or tape that helps reduce redness, itching, swelling, and irritation caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, rashes, and other inflammatory skin problems.
how_to_take: For cream, lotion, or ointment: Wash and dry your hands before and after use. Gently clean and dry the affected skin area. Apply a thin layer of the medicine to the affected area and rub it in gently. Do not cover with a bandage or wrap unless your doctor tells you to. For the tape: Clean and dry the skin completely before applying. Cut the tape to fit the affected area, press it firmly in place, and leave it on for 12 to 24 hours as directed. When removing, peel it back slowly to avoid skin irritation. Do not use on the face, groin, or underarms unless your doctor specifically tells you to.
dosing: Adults and children: Apply a thin layer to the affected area 2 to 3 times a day, or as directed by your doctor. For the tape, apply once every 12 to 24 hours. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not use more than recommended or use it for longer than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep the lid or cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children. Do not freeze the lotion or cream. Do not store in the bathroom where it can get warm and humid.
what_to_avoid: Do not get this medicine in your eyes, nose, or mouth. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use on broken, infected, or open skin unless directed by your doctor. Avoid using makeup or other skin products on the treated area unless your doctor approves. Do not use tight bandages, diapers, or plastic wrap over the treated area unless told to do so, as this can increase side effects. Avoid using this medicine for longer than your doctor recommends.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice: skin thinning, stretch marks, or skin color changes at the application site; increased redness, burning, or irritation that gets worse; signs of skin infection such as oozing, crusting, or warmth; acne-like bumps or unusual hair growth on the treated skin; blurred vision or eye pain; unusual weight gain, swelling, or extreme tiredness, which could be signs of the medicine being absorbed into your body; or if your condition does not improve after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement in redness, itching, and swelling within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement may take 1 to 2 weeks. If you do not see improvement after 2 weeks, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Use with caution in children. Children may absorb more of this medicine through the skin and are at higher risk for side effects. Do not use on a child's diaper area or cover with diapers or plastic pants. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed, and only on small areas for a short time. If breastfeeding, do not apply to the breast or nipple area. Elderly patients: Use with care as older skin may be more sensitive to side effects.
